A ten-year-old Black boy asked a Formula One boss for a job.
Ron Dennis wrote his answer in the boy's autograph book:
phone me in nine years.
But the boy's family had no money for racing.
His go-kart was fifth-hand.
So his dad fixed it up to look like new,
and worked several jobs at once to keep him racing.
At the track, he was often the only Black kid.
He later said he was bullied and racially abused,
and that he hid his tears so his dad wouldn't think he wasn't strong.
His dad told him:
always do your talking on the track.
So he did.
He kept winning.
Again, and again, and again.
Three years later, Dennis's team signed him.
And at twenty-three, two corners from the end of the season,
he passed one last car.
By a single point, he became world champion.
Racing for Ron Dennis.
The boy with the fifth-hand go-kart was Lewis Hamilton.
